# PR Review Sweep

A sweep reviews code that is **already merged**. Nothing here is a change under
review: there is no diff, no author to answer and no merge to gate. What a
sweep produces is a list of defects that were already in the tree, every one of
them tagged **Pre-existing**, so the people who read it can tell at a glance
that nobody introduced them today (REQ-021, AC-021-1).

It runs **when it is invoked**, and only then (AC-021-2, Constitution Rule 4).
This skill holds no timer, no schedule, no watcher and no background poll, and
ensemble's own `.github/workflows` carry no `schedule:` trigger. Recurrence is
the **host repository's** job (a workflow it owns, opted into and credentialed
by its maintainers) or **Foreman's**. The recommended cadence is **weekly**,
and a sweep starts with the sensitive areas (REQ-003).

This skill owns editable prose only (Constitution Rule 8): what is swept, in
what order, and how a sweep is reported. Every judgement that grades a claim --
sensitivity, rule resolution, depth bounds, slice coverage, ledger validity and
the verification vote -- is made by `pr-review-cli.js` (Rule 7), the same
binaries `pr-review-cycle` uses, so a sweep finding is held to exactly the
standard a PR finding is.

---

## Inputs

| Variable | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `SCOPE` | string[] | What to sweep: repository-relative paths, directories or globs. `['.']` sweeps the whole repository. An empty or unreadable scope is an error, never "everything by default". |
| `SWEEP_SHA` | string | The commit being swept -- a full 40- or 64-hex object id (`git rev-parse HEAD` on the branch under review), never a bare ref. Guidance is read from THIS commit: a sweep reviews merged code, so the merged tree is also the guidance in force (REQ-024). |
| `REQUESTED_BY` | string | Who asked: a maintainer's login, or the host automation's identity (for example `github-actions[bot]` from the repository's own workflow). Recorded in the report; it never changes what is reviewed. |
| `TIER` | `'low'` \| `'medium'` \| `'high'` (optional) | The depth this sweep is run at. Absent means `high` -- a sweep nobody bounded gets the deepest review, never the cheapest. |
| `MAX_PATHS` | number (optional) | A ceiling on how many paths this run examines, so a large repository can be swept in parts. The report names what was left for the next run; a truncated sweep is never reported as a complete one. |
| `TEST_COMMAND` | string (optional) | Recorded for reproduction instructions only. A sweep runs no tests and changes nothing. |

## Outputs

Exactly one of:

- **`SWEEP_COMPLETE`** -- the paths examined, the slices reviewed, the
  verified findings (every one tagged Pre-existing) and what was left for a
  next run.
- **`SWEEP_BLOCKED`** -- what could not be read or graded, and no findings
  list. A sweep that could not resolve its scope, its guidance or its
  verification reports that; it never reports a clean repository.

A sweep never writes code, never opens a PR, never pushes and never resolves
anybody's review thread. It reports.

---

## Resolve the CLI

Resolve `PR_REVIEW_CLI` per the tool-path-resolution skill
(`packages/development/skills/tool-path-resolution/SKILL.md`) for
`packages/development/lib/pr-review-cli.js`. If none of the 4 tiers resolve OR
`which node` fails: print `ERROR: Node.js and the PR review CLI
(lib/pr-review-cli.js) are required for deterministic review grading.` and
HALT.

Every subcommand is invoked the same way as in `pr-review-cycle`: `node
"$PR_REVIEW_CLI" <subcommand>` with one JSON payload on stdin and one JSON
object on stdout. A non-zero exit is `SWEEP_BLOCKED` naming the CLI error --
never a retry with guessed input.

---

## Algorithm

### Step 1 -- Resolve what will be swept

List the files under `SCOPE` at `SWEEP_SHA` with
`git ls-tree -r --name-only <SWEEP_SHA> -- <scope...>`, and their sizes with
`git ls-tree -r --long`. That list is the sweep set. A path that does not exist
at `SWEEP_SHA` is reported as not found, never silently dropped.

### Step 2 -- Resolve guidance from the swept commit (CLI `policy`, `rules`, `paths`)

Read the same guidance a PR review reads, from `SWEEP_SHA`:

- `node "$PR_REVIEW_CLI" policy` with `{ text, baseSha }`, where `text` is
  `git show <SWEEP_SHA>:REVIEW.md` (pass `null` when there is none -- the CLI
  then answers with the strict defaults, which is not the same as no policy);
- `node "$PR_REVIEW_CLI" rules` with
  `{ changedPaths, ruleFiles, rulesFileName, baseSha, sourceSha }`, where
  `changedPaths` is the sweep set and `ruleFiles` every `REVIEW.md` present at
  `SWEEP_SHA` (`git ls-tree -r --name-only <SWEEP_SHA>`), `baseSha` and
  `sourceSha` both `SWEEP_SHA`;
- `node "$PR_REVIEW_CLI" paths` with
  `{ changedPaths, declaration, codeowners, baseSha }`, the declaration and
  CODEOWNERS text read from `SWEEP_SHA`.

The `paths` result's `sensitive` and `high` lists are what Step 3 orders the
sweep by. A guidance call that answers `ok:false` is `SWEEP_BLOCKED`: a sweep
run under guidance nobody could read is not a sweep of this repository.

### Step 3 -- Sensitive areas first (REQ-003, AC-021-2)

Sweep in this order, and say in the report which band each finding came from:

1. every path in `paths.high`;
2. every path in `paths.sensitive` not already swept;
3. everything else in the sweep set.

When `MAX_PATHS` truncates the run, it truncates from the **end** of that
order: the sensitive bands are swept first and completely, and the report names
the paths left for the next run. A sweep that skipped a sensitive path reports
itself as incomplete, whatever else it found.

### Step 4 -- Depth and slices (CLI `depth`, `slices`)

Run `node "$PR_REVIEW_CLI" depth` with
`{ tier, requested, bounds, planned }` -- `tier` is `TIER` (absent means
`high`), `bounds` the policy's override when it carries one, and `planned` the
`{ reviewers, verifiers }` about to be dispatched. `violations` is binding
exactly as it is in `pr-review-cycle`: re-plan and call again until it is
empty, and never dispatch a plan the CLI refused.

Run `node "$PR_REVIEW_CLI" slices` with `{ paths, areas, threshold }`, where
`paths` is `[{ path, lines }]` for the sweep set (the file's line count, since
there is no diff to count), `areas` the directories of the rules files `rules`
applied plus the sensitive areas, and `threshold` the policy's slice threshold.
After the review, re-run it with `reviewed` and `changedPaths` to prove
coverage: an `uncovered` path is reported as unswept, never as clean.

### Step 5 -- Review with the same reviewers (fresh context, read-only)

Dispatch the reviewers `depth` allows -- at Standard or Deep **at least two**,
each a **fresh-context, read-only** subagent -- over the sweep set, slice by
slice, in the Step 3 order. Each reviewer is given only:

1. the files of its slice as they are at `SWEEP_SHA` (whole files: there is no
   diff here, and "what changed" is not the question),
2. the rules `applied` from Step 2 with the policy and sensitivity facts,
3. the repository guidance a reader would have (README, area `REVIEW.md`).

Not the authoring conversation, not this session, not an issue tracker's
opinion of the code. A reviewer reading what someone meant stops reviewing
what is there. No reviewer edits, stages, commits or pushes anything.

Record every candidate as a ledger entry exactly as `pr-review-cycle` Step 3
does -- `{ id, source, locationOrLink, severity, failureMode, disposition,
evidence, originalTextOrLink }` -- with **`severity` set to `Pre-existing` on
every one of them** (AC-021-1). `Pre-existing` is the third word of the
ledger's closed severity set (`Important`, `Nit`, `Pre-existing`), so the tag
is not a note in prose: `ledger` normalises it, the record comes back with
`preExisting: true`, and every consumer -- the report, the merge gate, the
metrics -- reads the same fact. It is set because the code was swept, never
because a reviewer judged a defect old.

Validate the batch with `node "$PR_REVIEW_CLI" ledger` (`action: 'validate'`,
then `dedupe`); a finding missing a required field is completed, never
dropped, and a finding that came back without `preExisting: true` was not
tagged -- fix its severity before reporting, rather than explaining the tag in
the summary.

A sweep still says how bad each finding is: carry the reviewer's own severity
judgement in the report (and in `failureMode` and `evidence`), so "pre-existing
and serious" is distinguishable from "pre-existing and cosmetic" without
re-tagging the finding as something a merge gate must answer.

Because `Pre-existing` findings never block a merge gate and are not
`isActionable` work on somebody else's PR, a sweep can never stop anybody's
PR: it informs, and the repository decides what to fix.

### Step 6 -- Verify before anything is reported (CLI `votes`)

Candidates are not findings until they are verified -- the same rule, the same
module and the same thresholds as a PR review. Run
`node "$PR_REVIEW_CLI" votes` with
`{ findings, depth, expectedVerifiers, verificationCapability }`: the depth's
verifiers (Standard 3, Deep 5), each a fresh-context subagent, and **never the
reviewer that raised the finding**. Report exactly `presented[]` -- `present`,
`disputed` and `unverified` -- with each finding's `authorLabel` verbatim. A
`filtered` finding stays in the ledger with its tally and is not reported as
something to fix.

On a runtime with no subagents, degrade exactly as `pr-review-cycle` does: one
single-pass review, `verificationCapability: false`, every finding
`unverified` / `no-subagent-capability`, and the reduced-review notice in the
report. A reduced sweep is never reported as a verified one.

### Step 7 -- Report

Report, in one place:

- `REQUESTED_BY`, `SWEEP_SHA` and the scope as given;
- the paths examined, in band order, and the slices reviewed;
- every verified finding with its band, its path and line, its severity, its
  `authorLabel` and the **Pre-existing** tag;
- what was left for the next run (`MAX_PATHS` truncation, uncovered slices,
  paths not found);
- the reduced-review notice when verification did not run.

Findings are **not** filed as PRs, commits or issues by this skill. A
maintainer (or the host automation that invoked it) decides what becomes work.

---

## Recurrence belongs to the host repository (AC-021-2)

This skill runs once per invocation. It never schedules itself, never waits for
a next run and never leaves a process behind.

A repository that wants a weekly sweep owns that schedule. `/ensemble-init-project`
offers to scaffold a workflow template for it -- **opt-in, never written
unless the user asks for it** -- and that template is the host's file from the
moment it lands: its cron, its runner, its credentials.

- The template needs the host's **own agent credentials** (an API key or token
  for whichever coding agent runs the review) because it drives a review agent
  in CI. That is a secret the repository already has, or chooses to add, for
  its own automation.
- The **core review path needs no new CI secret at all**: `pr-review-cycle`,
  `pr-merge` and this skill run inside a session a maintainer already
  authenticated, with the `gh` CLI that is already logged in. The sweep
  workflow is an optional convenience, not a dependency of the review process.

Ensemble ships no `schedule:` trigger of its own, and adding one here would
take ownership of recurrence away from the host repository and from Foreman
(Constitution Rule 4).

---

## Safety rules

- A sweep reports; it never changes code. No edit, no commit, no push, no PR,
  no resolved thread -- on any branch, including the one being swept.
- Every sweep finding carries the `Pre-existing` severity, so the ledger
  records `preExisting: true` for it. A sweep finding presented without that
  tag reads as a regression someone just introduced -- and would be counted
  as an open Important finding by the merge gate -- which is the one
  misunderstanding this skill exists to prevent.
- Sensitive areas are swept first and completely. A run that truncates names
  what it left; it never reports a partial sweep as a complete one.
- Verification is not optional. A candidate nobody verified is reported as
  `unverified`, never as a defect the repository must fix, and never dropped.
- Guidance is the swept commit's copy, read with `git show <SWEEP_SHA>:<path>`,
  never the working tree's.
- This skill never schedules, polls, waits for a trigger or recovers
  unattended. It is invoked, it runs, it reports, it ends.
